contexts.text: To explore the mysteries of faith by means of scientifics is as impossible...
Now, when they want to explore from headstrong reasoning what spirit is...
There is no exploration with the Lord, because He knows everything.
Therefore, when it is pleasing to the Lord, there is no need to explore by many things the quality of a Spirit; for he can be Known at his first coming.
Those who want to explore spiritual Truths from scientifics. Treated of.
Scientifics, by means of which they want to explore spiritual things. Treated of. AC 1163.
Those who by means of reasonings want to explore spiritual and celestial things.
Knowledge is such, that it desires nothing more than to introduce itself into heavenly things, and explore them...
So that there is no need that many things should be explored; his image is in every word and idea.
Everyone can see what quality of life he possesses, provided he explores the quality of his end.
Visitation is nothing but an exploration of the quality... and this exploration is expressed... by Jehovah's coming down and seeing.
Visitation or the exploration of their quality then precedes...
In the other life (the learned) have been examined as to what idea they had concerning the one God...
They explored the Land of Canaan... (See Canaan (Land of).)
He who wants to know the quality of his trust, let him explore in himself the affections, and the ends, and also the exercises of the life.
Exploration by Divine good. Signified.
Further exploration concerning innocence. Signified.
In connection with the initiation and conjunction of truth with good... there is the most exquisite exploration...
Exploration concerning the good of charity. Signified.
In these three verses it treats of the exploration of the truth which is to be initiated and conjoined with good... AC 3125.

The exploration exists with every man who is being reformed, and also with everyone who is receiving remains; but concerning this exploration man knows nothing whatever... This exploration is a most exquisite balancing, lest the least of falsity should be conjoined with good, or the least of truth with evil...
Exploration by the Divine Natural. Signified... To say, here, = to explore, because he interrogated him...
These things man is able to explore in himself, but he cannot do so in others; for the ends of everyone's affection are known to the Lord alone. Signified.
They clandestinely explore minds with a purpose of doing harm...
They who constitute the province of the kidneys, ureters, and bladder in the Grand Man are of such a genius, that they want nothing more than to explore and search out the quality of others...
The methods by which they explore or search out the minds of others are very numerous. Example(s).
0 Jehovah, examine my reins and my heart ()... To prove, examine, and search the reins = to prove, explore, and search the quantity and quality of truth...
(Joseph) said to them, Whence come ye = exploration.
Ye are spies () = that they are only after gain. Explained.
These truths of the Church, or those who are of such a character in the truths of the Church, are signified by spies coming to see the nakedness of the land. Explained.

That they are spies, may be sufficiently evident from the fact that they seek for nothing but blemishes in those who are in truths from good, in order to accuse and condemn... When once they have confirmed in themselves the doctrinal things of their own Church, are they anything but spies? for they laugh at and condemn the veriest truths if they come from any other source... because they have no affection of truth for its own sake, still less for the sake of life; but for the sake of gain. When such read the Word, they search it with the sole end of confirming doctrinal scientifics, for the sake of gain; and many of them search the Word in order to see the nakedness of the land... AC 5438. AC 5447.
Let Pharaoh live, ye are spies () = it is certain that ye have truths solely for the sake of gain. AC 5512. AC 5513.
The doctrinal things of the Church are first to be learned; and then exploration is to be made from the Word as to whether they are true...
When the Spirits of Mercury come to other Societies, they explore from them what they know...
After they have first been visited, that is, explored. Explorations take place to the intent that they themselves may apperceive that they cannot but be damned.
He who makes only a universal acknowledgement that he is a sinner, and does not examine himself, that is, see his sins...
After man has examined himself...
To try, here, = to explore.
It is this which one man explores in another... AC 10153:2.
He could dexterously explore everything of my thought...
Minister... here, = truth examining, exploring, and apperceiving.
The preacher who was with me was then explored, as to what idea he had concerning one God and three Persons...
In the other life an idea of thought... can be presented to view, and thereby everyone is explored as to the quality of his faith.
The learned have been explored...
In the World of Spirits... all are explored and prepared. HH 481:2.
These things are said to the end that man may examine himself...
(Novitiates) are examined by good Spirits...
They were examined as to whether their Knowledges resided in the memory, or in the life.
When they were examined it was found that they believed...
They were examined by the Angels as to what quality they were inwardly...
He is examined as to the quality of his cunning...
By means of this (equilibrium) all are examined as to their quality...
The man who examines himself in order to perform repentance must examine his thoughts and the intentions of his will... This is to examine himself.
To examine your lives and conversations by the rule of God's commandments.
It is a general principle in all religion that man ought to examine himself... DLife 106.
They who do not think about the evils in themselves, that is, who do not examine themselves... cannot but be ignorant of what evil is, and thus love it on account of its delight...
Still, all these things do not at all purify man, unless he examines himself...
As soon as, after examination, a man acknowledges evils to be sins against God...
Few examine themselves and see their sins; and he who does not see them is in the freedom of them...

It follows that not only is the external to be examined, but also the internal. If the external alone is examined, the man sees nothing but what he has actually committed... Thus he explores the evils of his body, and not those of his spirit; and yet in order for anyone to be reformed, the evils of the spirit must be explored... and the spirit can be explored only by a man attending to his thoughts, and especially to his intentions... Such is the examination of the internal man, from which, essentially, is the external man examined.

The meaning is... that man must examine himself, not only his deeds, but also his thoughts, and what he would do if he did not fear the laws and disgrace; especially what evils he regards in his spirit as allowable... In order that man may examine himself, an understanding has been given him, and this separate from the will...
a. He says, I am a sinner... but still he does not examine himself, and thus does not know any evil...
If a man reflects upon the evils in himself, which is the same as to examine himself...
And hast tried them that say they are apostles () = that they scrutinize those things which in the Church are called goods and truths. AE 100.
The novitiate Spirit is... carried into various Societies... and is examined as to whether he is affected with truths... or falsities...

I will keep thee from the hour of temptation that will come upon the whole world, to try them that dwell upon the earth () = that they will be protected and preserved in the day of the Last Judgment... They who underwent it were let into temptation, and were examined as to their quality.
Gold tried in the fire () = the good of celestial love.
Under Search, see this reference.
To take the Book and open it = to explore the states of life of all...
Preface. The exploration of those upon whom the Last Judgment is about to come. Treated of. AR 295. AR 302. AR 309. AR 324.
The exploration by the Lord of the state of the Church and of the life thence of those who are in His Spiritual Kingdom. Signified.
The exploration and disclosure of the state of the Church and of the life thence of those who are in faith alone. Signified. AR 397. AR 419. AR 464, Preface. AR 612, Preface.
The first Angel sounded = exploration and manifestation... AR 402.
Spiritual Divine truth... exploring and manifesting. Signified.
The final exploration and manifestation of the state of the Church... Signified.
The exploration and manifestation of the state of the Church after consummation. Signified.

The Reformed have a certain deep-seated... aversion to actual repentance, which is so great that they cannot compel themselves to examine themselves... It is as if horror invades them when they think of it.
These are they who do not examine themselves... For they say in their hearts, what is the need of examination...
Exploration of the quality of their works, that they were evil. Signified.
The reason a winepress = exploration. Explained, Illustrated.
That exploration was made from the Divine truths of the Word, as to the quality of the works... Signified.
The delights of these evils cannot be removed by the Lord unless the man examines himself...
On ascending into Heaven, all novitiates are examined as to the quality of their chastity. Described.
This confirmer was then sent to the Angels, who examined him as to his quality...
It is an established fact.
Everyone is examined there as to what the quality of his life has been.
If a man examines himself once or twice a year...
From His omnipotence and omniscience, God examines everyone after death...
We said to those who receive new-comers at the threshold, Examine these...
It can be examined and Known, whether...
It may be said that no one can explore the interiors of the mind of those with whom he is in company...
He was then sent to the Angel examiners... They reported that... he did not know that he had a single evil in himself, because he had never examined himself...
Such fear more than others to examine themselves...
The Knowledge of sin, and the examination of some sin in one's self, begin repentance. General article.
Unless a man examines the acts of his life...
What is better known... than that a man ought to examine himself...
Still, there are some who cannot examine themselves...
But they who know what sin is... and do not examine themselves...
That actual repentance is to examine one's self... General article.
True repentance is to examine not only the acts of one's life, but also the intentions of one's will. General article.
A man examines the intentions of his will, when he examines his thoughts...
To explore these two loves is very difficult. Explained.
They who do not examine themselves are like...
They who interiorly examine themselves are like...
They also perform repentance who do not examine themselves, but still desist from evils because they are sins... General article.
There are two duties incumbent on man after examination; supplication, and confession.
Thus is he introduced into the habit of examining himself...
Lead him away from... self-examination.
Some said, Who can examine himself when he knows himself to be mere sin?
Some said that whenever they intend to examine themselves, dread and terror seize them.
The quality of your internal man - of which you know nothing, because you have not examined yourselves, and after examination have not repented...
See Examine.

After he has stayed (in the other life) for some days, everyone is examined as to his quality, thus what had been his quality in the former world as to religion. When this has been done, the examiners report this to Heaven, and then he is transferred to those who are like him...
I have been told by the Angel examiners...
(On the examination of Souls after death.) SE 921. SE 926. SE 932. SE 2034. SE 2201, General article.
All who examine Souls and Spirits, and take pleasure in so doing, belong to the provinces of the secretories. SE 928. SE 959. SE 991. See SE 1239.
There are similar explorers in general, as in each of the Societies in particular.
They apply themselves to a Spirit, and constantly explore what he is thinking.
Although the investigators do not find out the causes, still they believe...
Such exploration is not permitted...
Thus the examiners themselves might be deceived...
To give one's self up to the investigation of such things...
On a certain kind of explorers, who excite the filthy things of evil Spirits.
The punishers have no need to explore others in this way; they know at once without any such exploration...
A method by which some gentiles from Asia explore whether they are tending to Heaven or to Hell.
The judges and examiners there at once perceive in what evil they are...
He was afterwards examined...
Others who are examined as to whether they believe truth who have not lived it...
At last that vast multitude was examined. Described.
On the fourth day after death he was called to judgment. (He was examined as to the members of his body.)
Examined also by a turning to the loves.
Many were examined... SE 5741. SE 5815.
1.2. They were first examined by being turned to lower things...
The examination lasted for hours...
The explorations of their quality are numerous. They are clearly seen by the Angels by means of turnings to the quarters. SE 5930. Explained.
He was examined as to what his quality had been in the world...
He was a most malicious explorer.
How Spirits are explored by means of ways, and from the seats in the house.
Such as explore... by means of affections inspired into the subject... and also by looks directed into various parts of the head...
There is another Hell... where are such as explore in order the things from the eyes to the chin, and down to the navel...
To try = to investigate, and scrutinize.
To try them that dwell upon the earth = visitation upon those who were in the former heaven...
Gold tried in the fire = genuine good, thus good from the Lord.
Exploration from the influx of the Lord into Heaven. Signified.
The sensuous man is in self-confidence and faith; for he cannot weigh and examine himself, because he does not think interiorly.
The examination of the men of the Church, as to the quality of the understanding of the Word that still remained with them. Signified. AE 620.
The method of visitation, that is, of exploration as to what is the quality of the Church as to truth and as to good. Signified, Explained.
That the external of the Word, and of the Church and of the worship thence, is not to be explored. Signified.
All who arrive in the Spiritual World are first examined as to the quality of the idea of God they have had...
Therefore, when Spirits are examined as to their quality, the place to which their thoughts extend themselves is traced out... AE 1093:end.
Exploration by the Lord concerning the state of the Church in general. Signified.
Announcement after exploration or visitation. Signified. AE 914. AE 917.
In the other life all are examined as to their quality in regard to their spiritual faith and life by means of an influx from Heaven concerning the Lord's Divine Human...
Unknown to him, they explore his thoughts... in. A vast multitude was examined... This examination seemed to be sudden and instantaneous...
Thus are new-comers into their heavenly Societies examined by the Angels.
Therefore, all are examined from their affection, and no one from his speech...
On the exploration of Spirits by means of marriage love.

Note. Examination. 1. If it regards the actions only, it discovers little... 2. If it regards also the thoughts and intentions, it then discovers more. 3. But if it explores what is accounted as sin, and what is not, it then discovers [all].
